To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Hfq and the ArcA regulator are involved in the activation of the SPI1 regulon in Salmonella serovar Typhi during the transition from exponential to stationary phase in a culture shaken in a test tube, but not when grown under stationary conditions.

the expression of SPI1 genes was highest during transition from the exponential phase to the stationary phase under shake culture conditions, and that Hfq and the ArcA regulon were involved in the stationary-phase dependent expression of SPI1 under shake culture conditions.
hfq and the arcA gene are required for the stationary phase-dependent induction of Salmonella pathogenity island 1 genes under shaking conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the regulators that are responsible for the stationary phase-dependent expression of SPI1 genes and the identification of the regulatory mechanisms involved in this expression.
the regulation of SPI1 genes and the identification of the regulatory genes involved in the stationary-phase-dependent activation of SPI genes under shaking conditions.
the identification of the factors involved in the stationary-phase-dependent activation of SPI-1 genes and the elucidation of their regulatory mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hfq and/or ArcA are involved with the stationary phase dependent activation of SPI1 under shaking conditions.
the stationary phase-dependent expression of SPI1 genes requires the accumulation of HilD protein, which is regulated by Hfq and Arca.
Hfq, IHF and ppGpp are required to maintain high levels of HilD expression during the stationary phase, and ArcA is required to maintain high expression of HilD in the late stationary phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hfq and/or ArcA are involved with the stationary phase dependent activation of SPI1 under shaking culture conditions.

the stationary phase-dependent regulation of SPI1 genes requires Hfq and Arc, and the expression of SPI1 genes in the early stationary growth phase is dependent on ppGpp and the presence of H-NS and IHF.
Hfq and the Arc system are involved in the activation of the SPI1 genes during stationary phase under shaking growth conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Hfq and arcA play an important role in the stationary phase-induced activation of SPI1 under shaking culture conditions and that the lack of Hfq and Arca causes a reduction in HilD accumulation in the early stationary growth phase.
the Hfq and Arc proteins are required to activate the SPI1 genes under conditions that mimic the intestinal environment.
the expression of SPI1 genes is regulated differently under shaking and standing conditions.
